title: Triangles: Angle Properties, Congruence and Similarity
seo_title: Grade 8 Triangles Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Revise properties and definitions of triangles in terms of their sides and angles; identify and write clear definitions of congruent and similar triangles; solve geometric problems involving unknown sides and angles in triangles using known properties and definitions, including the exterior angle of a triangle.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 8 triangles worksheets: angle sums, exterior angles, congruent triangles, similar triangles and scale factors. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles.
key_sub: Similar: equal angles, sides in ratio.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
  • Congruent triangles are identical: SSS, SAS, AAS or RHS.
  • Similar triangles have equal angles and sides in the same ratio.
  • Find the scale factor by dividing a side by its matching side.

Examples

Example

Similar triangles: 4 cm ↔ 10 cm, 6 cm ↔ ?

scale factor 10 ÷ 4 = 2,5

Answer: 6 × 2,5 = 15 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
360° in a triangleA triangle is 180°.
AAA for congruenceEqual angles only prove similarity.
Adding the scale factorMultiply by it.

items.q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 135°. One of the opposite interior angles is 78°. Find the other opposite interior angle.
items.e: Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles: 135 − 78 = 57°.

items.q: Can a triangle have two right angles?
c: No, because 90° + 90° = 180° leaves nothing for the third angle
items.e: No. Two right angles already make 180°.

items.q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 144°. One of the opposite interior angles is 44°. Find the other opposite interior angle.
items.e: Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles: 144 − 44 = 100°.

items.q: A triangle has interior angles of 45° and 25°. The side next to the third angle is extended. What is the exterior angle there?
items.e: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: 45 + 25 = 70°. (Or 180 − third angle 110°.)

items.q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 147°. One of the opposite interior angles is 39°. Find the other opposite interior angle.
items.e: Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles: 147 − 39 = 108°.

A triangle has interior angles of 58° and 46°. The side next to the third angle is extended. What is the exterior angle there?
items.e: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: 58 + 46 = 104°. (Or 180 − third angle 76°.)

items.q: A triangle has angles 50°, 60° and 70°. What type of triangle is it?
items.e: All angles are less than 90° and all different: acute-angled scalene.

items.q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 157°. One of the opposite interior angles is 37°. Find the other opposite interior angle.
items.e: Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles: 157 − 37 = 120°.

items.q: What is each angle in an equilateral triangle?
items.e: Three equal angles: 180 ÷ 3 = 60°.

No, because they would add to more than 180°

items.q: Both triangles have angles 40°, 60° and 80°. Are they definitely congruent?
c: No — they are similar, but could be different sizes
No, because the angles are different
items.e: Equal angles only prove the triangles are the same shape: similar, not necessarily congruent.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two angles and a matching side that is not between them are equal.
items.e: This is AAS.

items.q: Which of these does NOT prove two triangles are congruent?
items.e: Three equal angles only show the triangles are similar: AAA.

items.q: A shape is reflected. Is the image congruent to the original?
c: Only if the mirror line is vertical
items.e: Reflection keeps all lengths and angles, so yes.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two sides and the angle between them are equal.
items.e: This is SAS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two angles and the side between them are equal.
items.e: This is AAS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Both have a right angle, equal hypotenuses and one other equal side.
items.e: This is RHS.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 5, 7, 9 cm. Triangle 2 has sides 9, 5, 7 cm. Are they congruent?
c: No, the sides are in a different order
items.e: The same three side lengths in any order: yes, by SSS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? All three sides of one triangle are equal to all three sides of the other.
items.e: This is SSS.

items.q: Two right-angled triangles both have a hypotenuse of 13 cm and a side of 5 cm. Are they congruent?
c: Only if they face the same way
items.e: Right angle, hypotenuse, side: RHS.
